For any repairs, I'd strongly recommend getting a manual (pirate the factory service manual if possible) and tightening everything to torque spec. You'll generally need a 1/2, 3/8, and 1/4 torque wrench. If possible get used Snap-On ones off of craigslist or whatever. For the torque spec, they usually assume a clean bolt (use a wire brush) and you could use a drop of new engine oil.

Once you're at that level, I recommend a belt tension gauge like the "Gates 91107" or Krikit Gauge. Having the belts too lose isn't a big deal, but it will shred the belt sooner and spread rubber particles throughout the engine bay. Having it too tight will cause all the belt driven accessories (A/C, power steering, alternator, etc) to go early. Therefore, I always err on the side of lose.

You'll typically set the tension, run the vehicle for a specified time, and then reset the tension. New belts stretch, so be aware that the value when new will have to be adjusted at least once.

I'd also recommend anytime the belt is off you do a simple check on all the other belt driven components. Spin them slow by hand and it should be smooth and not catch. Try to pull and push on the pully (in and out and side to side). I wouldn't replace is just because it feels bad (unless your going on a cross country trip), but it will allow you to plan on the future.
